stages.name: Beyond GDP
stages.title: Beyond GDP
stages.sub: Why GDP alone cannot capture living standards, and how wellbeing is measured instead.

steps.q: GDP per head doubles over 30 years, while phones, hospitals and cars also get far better. Does GDP alone show that quality gain?
steps.right: No, it only counts the amount spent, not how much better things are
steps.wrong: Yes, a higher GDP figure already reflects better quality
steps.hint: GDP adds up spending. Does spending the same £500 on an old phone versus a much better new phone show up differently?

steps.q: Since the 1950s real incomes in rich countries have risen a lot, yet reported happiness has barely moved. Does higher income guarantee happiness?
steps.right: No, happiness does not keep rising with income
steps.wrong: Yes, happiness rises in line with income
steps.hint: Think about the survey result: income line goes up steadily, happiness line stays flat.

steps.q: Since GDP misses quality and income doesn't clearly raise happiness, would a statistics office want another measure?
steps.right: Yes, it would want to measure other aspects of life directly
steps.wrong: No, it would just keep publishing GDP figures
steps.hint: If money alone doesn't capture wellbeing, what else could be tracked and published?

steps.q: To capture how well people's lives are going, would one money question do, or would surveys need several separate areas?
steps.right: You would need several separate areas
steps.wrong: One single question would cover it
steps.hint: Think about everything that affects how someone's life is going besides their pay.

steps.prompt: Drag and drop the 4 key terms in the order they build on each other.

steps.q: Some survey areas ask people to rate their life satisfaction, health, family and friendships. Are they about personal life or the wider economy?
steps.right: How someone personally feels and connects
steps.wrong: The state of the wider economy
steps.hint: Life satisfaction, health, relationships - are these about the person, or about GDP and jobs?
